title: QAC0 Can Prepare Every Logarithmic-Qubit State
authors: Lucas Gretta, Meghal Gupta, Malvika Raj Joshi
abstract: $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ is the class of constant-depth $\mathrm{poly}(n)$-ancilla circuits obtained by extending $\mathsf{QNC}^0$, the class of local circuits, to include nonlocal interactions via arbitrary width Toffoli gates. It is believed to be weaker than its counterpart, $\mathsf{QNC}^0_f$, obtained by including arbitrary-width FANOUT gates instead ($\mathsf{QAC}^0 \subseteq \mathsf{QNC}^0_f$ [Moo99]).   In this note, we show that every $O(\log n)$-qubit state can be exactly and cleanly prepared by a $\mathrm{poly}(n)$-ancilla $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit. Previous known $\mathrm{poly}(n)$-ancilla circuits for arbitrary such states are only known via additional access to either FANOUT or QRAM (indexing) gates [Ros21b, GGJ26b], neither of which are known to be in $\mathsf{QAC}^0$. Equivalently, prior constructions of arbitrary $n$-qubit states in $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ require doubly exponential size and we obtain an exponential factor improvement.
summary: This paper proves that the quantum circuit model $\mathsf{QAC}^0$, which uses constant-depth circuits with multi-qubit Toffoli gates, can efficiently prepare any arbitrary quantum state whose size scales logarithmically with the system size. This result is significant because it achieves this feat without requiring access to powerful, non-native gates like FANOUT or QRAM, offering an exponential improvement over previous constructions.
main_problem: To demonstrate that the computational model $\mathsf{QAC}^0$, based on constant-depth circuits with multi-qubit Toffoli gates, is powerful enough to prepare arbitrary $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$-qubit quantum states.
main_result: The authors prove that every $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$-qubit state can be exactly and cleanly prepared using only a polynomial number of ancilla qubits and a $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit.
method: The proof utilizes a combination of parallel amplification techniques, building upon prior work, and constructing the state preparation through sequential steps involving controlled-SWAP gates.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the quantum circuit model $\mathsf{QAC}^0$, which consists of constant-depth circuits extended from local interactions by arbitrary-width Toffoli gates. This model is compared against $\mathsf{QNC}^0_f$ (using FANOUT gates) and models requiring QRAM access.
key_observables: The ability to prepare a target state $|\psiangle$ of size $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$ qubits.
important_parameters: The circuit depth is constant, and the ancilla count is polynomial in $n$. The state size is $\mathcal{O}(\log n)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of the EXACT1 gate within the $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ framework and relies on established amplitude amplification techniques.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the main theorem by showing the state preparation is achievable via a sequence of steps: weak approximation, amplitude amplification, and final clean-up, demonstrating an exponential improvement over prior resource requirements.
why_interesting: This work provides a significant theoretical result regarding the computational power of restricted quantum circuit models, which is foundational for understanding the limits of quantum computation in physical implementations.
